anxious.speaker: Jeffrey R. Holland
anxious.text: Don't you quit. You keep walking. You keep trying. There is help and happiness ahead. Some blessings come soon, some come late, and some don't come until heaven; but for those who embrace the gospel of Jesus Christ, they come.

anxious.speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
anxious.text: God's love is not contingent upon perfection or flawlessness. He loves us as we are, in all our struggles and imperfections.

anxious.speaker: Russell M. Nelson
anxious.text: When we are on the covenant path, we are safe.

anxious.speaker: Sharon Eubank
anxious.talk: Christ: The Light That Shines in Darkness
anxious.text: If you are lonely, Christ is your companion. If you feel you've made too many mistakes, He is your redemption. When you are discouraged, He is your hope.

anxious.speaker: Thomas S. Monson
anxious.text: The Lord has promised, 'I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.' May we remember that life is filled with detours and dead ends, trials and challenges of every kind. Each of us has likely had times when distress, anguish, and despair almost consumed us. Yet we are here—we have made it thus far.

anxious.speaker: Neal A. Maxwell
anxious.text: God is not only aware of our individual circumstances but cares about each of us individually. The very hairs on our head are numbered.

anxious.speaker: Michelle D. Craig
anxious.text: God wants to work in and through us, with all of our flaws and limitations. He doesn't expect perfection yet, just progress.

anxious.speaker: Chieko N. Okazaki
anxious.text: Jesus knows what it is like to be tired and thirsty. He knows what it is like to feel abandoned. He knows what it is like to face seemingly impossible tasks.

exhausted.speaker: Jeffrey R. Holland
exhausted.text: Hold on, keep trying, God loves you, things will improve.

exhausted.speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
exhausted.text: It is not enough that we are busy. The question is, what are we busy about? We would do well to slow down a little, focus on the significant, and lift our eyes toward what matters most.

exhausted.speaker: Russell M. Nelson
exhausted.talk: Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives
exhausted.text: In coming days, it will not be possible to survive spiritually without the guiding, directing, comforting, and constant influence of the Holy Ghost.

exhausted.speaker: Neal A. Maxwell
exhausted.text: Patient endurance is to be distinguished from merely being 'acted upon.' Endurance is more than pacing up and down within the cell of our circumstance; it is not the acceptance of futility.

exhausted.speaker: Henry B. Eyring
exhausted.text: The Lord had promised that He would be with us as we faced the steep climb. He is with us. The Holy Ghost has been sent to comfort and to guide.

exhausted.speaker: David A. Bednar
exhausted.talk: Bear Up Their Burdens with Ease
exhausted.text: The Savior is not a crutch; He is the only way by which we can fulfill our divine potential.

exhausted.speaker: Virginia H. Pearce
exhausted.text: Our Heavenly Father does not expect us to carry our burdens entirely alone. That is why He gave us the Savior, the Comforter, and each other.

exhausted.speaker: Sheri Dew
exhausted.text: The Lord's promise is not that we will be saved from our trials, but that we will be sustained through them.

distracted.speaker: Russell M. Nelson
distracted.text: In coming days, it will not be possible to survive spiritually without deliberately choosing to hear Him above the noise of the world.

distracted.speaker: David A. Bednar
distracted.text: The adversary is pleased when we disconnect from the people we love and from the things that matter most. Sometimes, without even realizing it, we allow the things of the world to crowd out the things of eternity.

distracted.speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
distracted.text: We have to forego some good things in order to choose others that are better or best.

distracted.speaker: Neal A. Maxwell
distracted.talk: Overcome... Even As I Also Overcame
distracted.text: When we are unduly impatient with an omniscient God's timing, we really are suggesting that we know best.

distracted.speaker: Henry B. Eyring
distracted.text: Before I went to sleep, I would ask myself, 'Have I seen the hand of God reaching out to touch us or our children or our family today?' As I kept at it, something began to happen. I saw it everywhere.

distracted.speaker: Brad Wilcox
distracted.text: The Atonement is not just for big sins. It is for every moment when we feel inadequate, distracted, or lost.

distracted.speaker: M. Russell Ballard
distracted.talk: Be Still and Know That I Am God
distracted.text: We live in a noisy world. We have to do our part in carving out moments of stillness where the Holy Spirit can speak to us.

sad.speaker: Jeffrey R. Holland
sad.text: Do not give up. Do not give in. This too shall pass.

sad.speaker: Thomas S. Monson
sad.text: This is our one opportunity to live and to learn, to grow and to love, to give and to serve. Let us not miss the experience.

sad.speaker: Henry B. Eyring
sad.text: God will not leave us alone in the darkness. He loves us. He sees our suffering and He will send light.

sad.speaker: Chieko N. Okazaki
sad.text: Jesus wants to be with you in your pain. He is not distant from your suffering. He has walked this road.

sad.speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
sad.text: God is fully aware that you and I are not perfect. He knows it, and He loves us anyway.

sad.speaker: Neal A. Maxwell
sad.talk: Apply the Atoning Blood of Christ
sad.text: The Savior took upon Himself our infirmities, including our sorrow. He understands not just our failures, but our feelings.

sad.speaker: Patrick Kearon
sad.talk: He Is Risen with Healing in His Wings
sad.text: In your most honest, painful moments, when the loss feels unbearable, know that He bore it first — for you.

sad.speaker: Virginia H. Pearce
sad.text: We are not alone in our grief. The Lord grieves with us, and He grieves for us, and He weeps.

frustrated.speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
frustrated.text: When we feel frustrated, it is often a signal that we care deeply. Channel that energy. Redirect it toward building, not tearing down.

frustrated.speaker: Russell M. Nelson
frustrated.text: The Savior's example is the ultimate rebuke of our frustrations. He never let impatience take His eyes off who He was there to love.

frustrated.speaker: Neal A. Maxwell
frustrated.text: Patience is not passive resignation, nor is it failing to act in the face of injustice. Patience means active waiting and enduring.

frustrated.speaker: Jeffrey R. Holland
frustrated.text: We don't need to be jealous of each other's progress. Stop comparing your test with someone else's. God has a unique plan for you.

frustrated.speaker: Thomas S. Monson
frustrated.text: Let us fill our hearts with love. It is the antidote to anger, the salve for frustration, and the foundation of peace.

frustrated.speaker: David A. Bednar
frustrated.text: Meekness is the disposition to submit to what the Lord wills, even when that feels like a defeat to the natural man.

overwhelmed.speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
overwhelmed.text: We can spend a lifetime whirling about at a feverish pace, checking off one task after another, and never stop to ask ourselves: what are the things that truly matter most?

overwhelmed.speaker: Jeffrey R. Holland
overwhelmed.talk: Cast Not Away Therefore Your Confidence
overwhelmed.text: Don't panic and retreat from the light. Don't forget how things looked in the dark. Lessons learned in darkness are essential.

overwhelmed.speaker: Russell M. Nelson
overwhelmed.text: Joy is a gift for the faithful. The world will taunt you and tell you joy is impossible under such conditions. The world is wrong.

overwhelmed.speaker: Wendy Nelson
overwhelmed.talk: Becoming the Person You Were Born to Be
overwhelmed.text: You were not sent here to be overwhelmed. You were sent here to overcome.

overwhelmed.speaker: Henry B. Eyring
overwhelmed.talk: Spiritual Preparedness: Start Early and Be Steady
overwhelmed.text: When the troubles are many and the solutions seem impossible, remember that the Lord knows your situation and He will provide a way.

overwhelmed.speaker: David A. Bednar
overwhelmed.talk: Bear Up Their Burdens with Ease
overwhelmed.text: The enabling power of the Atonement of Christ strengthens us to do and be good and to serve beyond our own individual desire and natural capacity.

overwhelmed.speaker: Neal A. Maxwell
overwhelmed.text: The Lord will not only give us strength equal to our tasks, but He will make heavy burdens feel light.

numb.speaker: Jeffrey R. Holland
numb.text: If you are a loved one of someone who is in this dark place, cherish them, be with them, don't stigmatize them. Walk with them toward the light.

numb.speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
numb.text: No matter how dark your days may seem, no matter how insignificant you may feel, no matter how overshadowed you think you may be, your Heavenly Father has not forgotten you.

numb.speaker: Sharon Eubank
numb.talk: Christ: The Light That Shines in Darkness
numb.text: Sometimes the darkness lasts so long we forget what light felt like. He hasn't forgotten. He is still there, still calling your name.

numb.speaker: Patrick Kearon
numb.talk: He Is Risen with Healing in His Wings
numb.text: Jesus Christ descended below all things, which means there is no depth of despair, no darkness, no numbness, where He has not already been.

numb.speaker: Henry B. Eyring
numb.text: Start looking for the small signs. God leaves fingerprints everywhere, especially in the moments when we feel nothing.

numb.speaker: Brad Wilcox
numb.text: Grace is not just for the sinful. It is for the weary, the empty, the ones who have nothing left to give.

happy.speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
happy.text: Could I suggest that we see gratitude as a disposition, a way of life that stands independent of our current situation? In other words, I'm suggesting that instead of being thankful for things, we focus on being thankful in our circumstances.

happy.speaker: Thomas S. Monson
happy.text: Let us relish life as we live it, find joy in the journey, and share our love with friends and family.

happy.speaker: Russell M. Nelson
happy.text: When the focus of our lives is on Jesus Christ and His gospel, we can feel joy regardless of what is happening—or not happening—in our lives.

happy.speaker: Jeffrey R. Holland
happy.text: Let heaven's light in. Sing a song of thanksgiving today, even if your voice is imperfect. The Lord loves the unpolished melody of a grateful heart.

happy.speaker: Henry B. Eyring
happy.text: As I counted my blessings, I began to see that the good in my life far outweighed the difficult. God is generous beyond measure.

happy.speaker: Cecil O. Samuelson
happy.talk: What Does It Mean to Be a BYU Student?
happy.text: You have been blessed beyond what most on this earth will ever know. Let that sink in—and then let it pour back out.

hopeful.speaker: Jeffrey R. Holland
hopeful.text: Don't look back. God doesn't live there. He lives ahead of you — in your future, in your potential, in your becoming.

hopeful.speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
hopeful.text: Hope is one leg of a three-legged stool, together with faith and charity. These three stabilize our lives regardless of the rough or uneven surfaces we might encounter at the turns and crossroads of mortality.

hopeful.speaker: Russell M. Nelson
hopeful.text: The future of this Church is extraordinarily bright. And the future for each of you is equally bright, if you choose it.

hopeful.speaker: Neal A. Maxwell
hopeful.talk: Hope Through the Atonement of Jesus Christ
hopeful.text: Hope, in turn, is nurtured by the atonement of Jesus Christ. He paid the ransom for our sins and opened the door of hope.

hopeful.speaker: Sharon Eubank
hopeful.text: God has a magnificent plan for you. Not in spite of your circumstances, but very often because of them.

hopeful.speaker: Henry B. Eyring
hopeful.text: The assurance that comes from keeping covenants brings hope. You can face the road ahead with confidence because you are not walking it alone.

hopeful.speaker: Patrick Kearon
hopeful.text: Because He suffered and rose again, we too can rise. Whatever storm you face, He has already faced it and overcome it for you.

grateful.speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
grateful.text: The choice to be grateful is a choice to see clearly. It doesn't deny the hard things — it simply refuses to let them be the whole story.

grateful.speaker: Thomas S. Monson
grateful.text: We can lift ourselves and others as well when we refuse to remain in the realm of negative thought and instead exercise our innate capability to choose and to refocus on our blessings.

grateful.speaker: Henry B. Eyring
grateful.text: As I began to write down the blessings of the day, I stopped thinking so much about my troubles and began to see the fingerprints of God all over my life.

grateful.speaker: Russell M. Nelson
grateful.talk: The Correct Name of the Church
grateful.text: To be a member of this Church is one of the greatest blessings that could come to any person in this life.

grateful.speaker: Bonnie L. Oscarson
grateful.text: Count your blessings and name them one by one — you will find that your God has done and is doing more than you know.

grateful.speaker: Terryl Givens
grateful.text: Gratitude is not a passive acknowledgment of blessings. It is an active orientation of the heart toward the Source of all good things.
